ety.text: Disputed. Traditionally, the word has been connected with ulcus (“sore”), with the term following a semantic development of "to grow sores (against someone)" > "to avenge one's griefs." De Vaan considers this etymology uncompelling. The LIV suggests a possible derivation from Proto-Indo-European *h₂l̥ksḱéti, from *h₂elk- (“to protect, ward off”). However, De Vaan considers this etymology semantically uncompelling.
